items.description: BeagleBone AI-64 board with its supplied heatsink, a recorded stable identity, and no visible connector or PCB damage.

supported_examples.notes: The sole reference board. Record the PCB revision and SoC silicon revision separately for every observed unit.

acceptance_checks.criterion: The physical marking and discovered board identity identify a BeagleBone AI-64.
The supplied heatsink is present and the PCB, power, microSD, Ethernet, fan, and selected UART connectors have no visible damage.
A stable asset ID, board EEPROM serial and revision, and live SoC revision are recorded; missing exported fields are explicitly unavailable rather than inferred.

automatic_discovery.source: Board EEPROM name, serial number, and revision exposed by the running system
automatic_discovery.limitations: The EEPROM access path is image and kernel dependent; the PCB revision does not identify the SoC silicon revision.

automatic_discovery.source: /sys/devices/soc* machine, family, soc_id, revision, and serial_number attributes
automatic_discovery.limitations: Individual sysfs attributes can be absent and must be recorded as unavailable.
Device-tree identity describes the selected DTB and is corroborating evidence, not a unique asset identity.

evidence.claim: The BeagleBone AI-64 uses a TDA4VM, has 4 GB LPDDR4, 16 GB eMMC, microSD, two 3.3 V debug UARTs, Gigabit Ethernet, a fan connector, and a supplied heatsink.
The board EEPROM format includes board name, revision, and serial number.
Linux defines SoC machine, family, serial_number, soc_id, and revision attributes under sysfs when a platform exports them.

items.description: Dedicated regulated 5 V, center-positive supply with at least 4 A rated output and a connector physically qualified on the reference board.

supported_examples.notes: Candidate dedicated supply with 5.5 mm OD/2.1 mm ID center-positive plug. Physical fit and loaded stability must pass before fleet purchase because the board documentation does not publish barrel dimensions.

acceptance_checks.criterion: The supply label states regulated 5 V DC output at 4 A or greater; no higher-voltage-only supply is accepted.
Barrel polarity is center-positive and connector fit is secure on the sampled board.
The board remains powered without reset or undervoltage indication under the qualification workload with the selected fan and normal bench peripherals.

evidence.claim: The board requires a 5 V supply and detailed BeagleBoard guidance specifies more than 3 A; attached peripherals can increase demand.
BeagleBoard documents at least 5 V/3 A through a matching center-positive barrel connector or USB-C for the AI-64.
The candidate supply is specified as regulated 5 V/4 A with a center-positive barrel plug.

items.description: Active forced-air assembly for the supplied heatsink, electrically and mechanically qualified on the reference board and used for all course workloads and measurements.

supported_examples.notes: Candidate 40 x 40 x 10 mm, 5 V, four-wire PWM/tach fan. It is not fleet-qualified until its mounting, board-side harness, header load, startup, tachometer, PWM behavior, and thermal result pass the listed checks.

acceptance_checks.criterion: The assembly is wired for the observed board revision with GND, 5 V, tachometer, and PWM on the verified pins and stays within the qualified header or external-supply current limit.
The fan is securely mounted, directs air across the supplied heatsink, clears cables and moving parts, and cannot short the board.
The fan starts reliably at power-on; tachometer and PWM response are observed when board-header control is used, or an approved always-on external-power limitation is recorded.
The assembly meets the project temperature and non-throttling envelope under the later sustained qualification workload.

automatic_discovery.source: Kernel hwmon or platform fan tachometer interface when exported by the selected image
automatic_discovery.limitations: The board documentation does not establish the final Linux fan driver or sysfs path; visual or instrumented observation remains required if no tachometer interface is exported.
Temperature does not prove airflow or fan identity; sensor mapping and throttling thresholds must be captured with the selected kernel.

evidence.claim: The board includes a heatsink and exposes a PWM-controllable four-pin fan connector.
The revision-B1 schematic identifies the four fan signals as GND, 5 V, tachometer, and PWM.
The candidate fan is a 5 V, four-wire PWM/tachometer model with a 0.07 A maximum input current.

items.description: Traceable, genuine microSD media used as the station working card and accepted by capacity, endurance, identity, and scratch write/read/hash checks.

supported_examples.notes: Reference 64 GB UHS-I U1/Class 10/A1 high-endurance media. Purchase only through a traceable source and qualify actual samples.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Manufacturer, model, nominal and observed capacity, kernel-exposed CID/serial when available, purchase source, and asset label are recorded without relying on /dev/sdX enumeration.
Observed capacity is at least 32 GB and the final course image later leaves at least the frozen free-space margin.
The exact product family has a manufacturer endurance specification and meets Class 10/U1 or better.
A destructive scratch-card full-device write/read verification passes before the card enters service; the exact target requires separate destructive approval.

automatic_discovery.source: udev properties, /dev/disk/by-id links, and explicitly selected lsblk columns
automatic_discovery.limitations: USB storage serials and by-id links are optional; a block name alone is never a stable or sufficient flashing identity.

automatic_discovery.source: Kernel MMC CID, CSD, name, serial, and capacity attributes when the card is installed in the board
automatic_discovery.limitations: Availability and path depend on the kernel, reader path, and whether the card is connected through native MMC or USB.

evidence.claim: The board supports microSD as a boot source and supports larger-capacity cards.
SDHC spans more than 2 GB through 32 GB and SDXC spans more than 32 GB through 2 TB.
The reference Kingston card is specified as 64 GB, UHS-I U1/Class 10/A1 high-endurance media.

items.description: Linux-compatible USB microSD reader that exposes media as a removable block device and passes the exact-target identity and scratch-media tests.

supported_examples.notes: Transport-compatible candidate with Linux support. The manufacturer does not promise a unique USB or storage serial, so sampled units must pass the stable-identity acceptance check before automated flashing.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Linux enumerates one inserted card as exactly one new whole removable USB block device with the expected capacity and no mounted filesystems before a write.
The sampled reader exposes a non-placeholder unique serial and stable /dev/disk/by-id link; duplicate or missing identities fail automated-flashing acceptance.
A /dev/disk/by-path link is recorded as a secondary physical-port check and is never substituted for a unique reader identity when benches can be recabled.
Read and separately approved scratch-media write/read/hash tests complete without I/O errors or disconnects.

automatic_discovery.source: udev USB vendor, product, serial, and stable device links
automatic_discovery.limitations: A catalogue model does not prove that every unit exposes a unique serial; identities must be sampled and checked for duplicates.

automatic_discovery.source: A before/after udev and lsblk comparison after udev settles
automatic_discovery.limitations: Discovery stays read-only and does not authorize writing; Task 007 must refuse ambiguous, mounted, or unstably identified targets.

evidence.claim: The candidate reader supports microSDHC/microSDXC, UHS-I/UHS-II, USB 3.2 Gen 1, and Linux.
Upstream lsblk documentation warns that default output can change and recommends explicit columns and udev settling for recently added devices.
Systemd persistent-storage rules create by-id links from supplied device serial properties and by-path links from connection topology.

items.description: Genuine 3.3 V USB-to-TTL serial adapter with a stable USB identity and a revision-qualified, keyed three-wire GND/TX/RX board harness.

supported_examples.notes: Reference 3.3 V UART cable with a factory-programmed unique USB serial. Its six-pin 0.1-inch termination requires a separately qualified three-wire board adapter, and its 5 V VCC wire must remain disconnected.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Adapter UART I/O is 3.3 V TTL; adapter TX connects to board RX, adapter RX to board TX, and GND to GND with VCC, RTS, and CTS disconnected.
The keyed, strain-relieved harness physically fits the observed board revision and its verified pin order is recorded; 1.25 mm and 1.5 mm connector descriptions are not treated as interchangeable.
USB vendor, product, unique serial, and stable device link are recorded and remain stable across reconnects.
The selected Linux console produces valid 115200 8N1 output from power-on without hardware handshaking or framing errors.

automatic_discovery.source: udev USB vendor, product, serial, and stable serial-device links
automatic_discovery.limitations: USB identity does not prove 3.3 V signaling, wiring, connector fit, or that the observed port is the selected Linux console.
Successful capture is image and port dependent and does not authorize board power or storage changes.

evidence.claim: The board exposes two three-pin 3.3 V TTL debug UARTs with TX/RX only, and the documented console settings are 115200 8N1 without handshaking.
The board design documentation identifies the UART header signals as GND, RXD, and TXD.
The reference adapter uses 3.3 V UART I/O, has a factory-programmed unique USB serial, and also exposes a 5 V VCC wire.
The revision-B1 schematic names the board connector B3B-ZR, which conflicts with the current cable guide's 1.25 mm PicoBlade description and requires physical qualification.

items.description: One Cat5e-or-better patch lead and one reachable 100/1000BASE-T network port per station, with link, address, route, and SSH behavior recorded as site facts.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Patch lead is Cat5e or better, latches securely, has no visible damage, and terminates at the recorded switch or network port.
Carrier is present, the negotiated rate is at least 100 Mbit/s and preferably 1000 Mbit/s, and reconnect restores the link.
Permanent/current MAC, IP addressing method and address, route from the agent workstation, and SSH host identity are recorded and pass reachability checks.

automatic_discovery.source: Kernel network interface attributes and ethtool link information
automatic_discovery.limitations: Negotiated link state does not identify cable make, physical route, VLAN, DHCP policy, firewall policy, or spare switch capacity.

automatic_discovery.source: Interface permanent/current MAC, assigned address, route, neighbor state, and SSH host key
automatic_discovery.limitations: Addressing and reachability are site-dependent and must be observed in the target lab.

evidence.claim: The BeagleBone AI-64 exposes a Gigabit Ethernet RJ45 interface.
BeagleBoard documents a standard 100 Mbit/s Ethernet cable as sufficient for basic connectivity.

items.description: Dedicated, labeled, normally offline high-endurance microSD containing a hash-verified course recovery image that cold-boots a reference board through the documented boot-button path.

supported_examples.notes: Use the same qualified high-endurance family as working media, but dedicate and label the recovery card and normally keep it offline.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Card asset ID, manufacturer, model, capacity, media identity when exported, state, and compatible board revisions are recorded.
Canonical image URL/build identity and SHA-256, write timestamp, writing tool identity, target stable identity, and post-write verification result match the release record.
The card cold-boots a reference board through the boot-button microSD path and reports the expected image identity without modifying eMMC.
After verification the card is labeled, marked sealed or checked-out in inventory, and stored offline with its canonical image and hash available separately.

automatic_discovery.source: The same udev, stable block link, lsblk, and native MMC identity sources used for working media
automatic_discovery.limitations: Discovery cannot establish image correctness or authorize a write; a separate exact-target approval and post-write verification are required.

automatic_discovery.source: The booted image's immutable build metadata and the release SHA-256 manifest
automatic_discovery.limitations: Image identity is accepted only after a cold microSD boot; filesystem contents observed through a reader alone do not prove bootability.

evidence.claim: Holding the boot button while removing and reapplying power selects microSD boot and provides the documented eMMC update/recovery path.
The reference Kingston card is specified as 64 GB high-endurance media suitable for repeated image use.
